title: Dithered sign expectation and its inverse
purpose: Compute the mean of sign(x + noise) for Gaussian or uniform dither, 2 Phi(x/sigma) - 1 or x/a, check it against a seeded Monte Carlo estimate with its standard error, and invert it to recover x from an observed mean of one-bit readings.

entry_points.name: sign_expectation
entry_points.arguments: x: number; sigma > 0 (Gaussian standard deviation or uniform half-width); dither: gaussian or uniform

entry_points.name: monte_carlo_sign_expectation
entry_points.arguments: x; sigma; samples (1 to 2000000); seed (non-negative integer); dither

entry_points.name: recover_offset
entry_points.arguments: mean_sign: observed mean of dithered signs; sigma; dither
entry_points.returns: the x whose dithered sign has that mean

assumptions: The dither is independent of x and of the other draws, with the stated distribution and scale.
sign(0) = 0; with continuous dither this happens with probability 0.
guarantees: Gaussian: E[sign(x + sigma Z)] = 2 Phi(x / sigma) - 1, computed as erf(x / (sigma sqrt 2)).
Uniform on [-a, a]: x / a inside [-a, a], sign(x) outside.
recover_offset inverts sign_expectation; the Monte Carlo standard error is sqrt((1 - m^2) / N).

known_wrong.name: not_the_undithered_sign
known_wrong.why: Without dither the mean sign is 1 for every positive x and the magnitude is lost.

known_wrong.name: not_the_small_signal_slope
known_wrong.why: Extrapolating the slope sqrt(2/pi) at zero overstates the mean once x is comparable to sigma.

limits: Gaussian and uniform dither only, with a known scale. Inversion of the Gaussian form needs a mean strictly inside (-1, 1) and loses precision near the ends, where the curve is flat. The Monte Carlo check uses a Box-Muller generator on random() and is a consistency check, not a proof.
technique_references: Gaussian error function identity 2 Phi(z) - 1 = erf(z / sqrt 2)
